pins.name: 5V
pins.notes: Use VIN for a few LEDs; a separate 5 V supply for more (up to 60 mA per LED)

pins.name: DIN
pins.notes: Data in. Add a 330 Ω resistor; a 3.3 V to 5 V level shifter makes it reliable

gotchas.text: Each LED draws up to about 60 mA at full white: 30 LEDs need about 1.8 A, more than USB gives. Power the strip from its own 5 V supply and connect the grounds.
Put a 300 to 500 Ω resistor in the data line and a large capacitor (about 1000 µF) across the strip’s supply.
At 5 V the data input needs at least 0.7 × 5 V = 3.5 V to read HIGH. A 3.3 V board often works but not always: a level shifter (74AHCT125) makes it reliable.
